translations.answer: If the environment is consistent with the original post, do not batch modify the model. The `-1.0` value is a sentinel value used by DART; the validation regression in 6.16.5 incorrectly triggered an alert. DART PR #2493 has been merged and the release record points to 6.16.6; the original author confirmed the alert disappeared after upgrading to DART 6.16.6 via Homebrew. Only continue checking model data when the parameter is not this sentinel, but instead NaN/Inf or custom exception values.
translations.applicability: Applies to the `-1` sentinel warning in Gazebo Ionic 9.5.0 / DART 6.16.5; other error values require further investigation.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict, and there is formal documentation or precise independent replication.
translations.details.attempts.0: Explicitly setting `slip1=0` and `slip2=0` in SDF can make a single model silent, but it does not resolve large Fuel models; `-v 0` is ineffective.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First check the DART version; confirm the log parameter value is exactly the sentinel `-1`, not NaN/Inf or explicit invalid configuration.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Upgrade to 6.16.6 containing DART PR #2493; the patch silently returns a default value for negative sentinel, and only retains the warning for NaN/Inf.
translations.details.environments.0: macOS Homebrew; Gazebo Ionic 9.5.0; DART 6.16.5 triggers, author upgraded to DART 6.16.6 and retested.
translations.details.limits.0: The fix is specific to the sentinel being exactly negative; if input is NaN/Inf or custom non-expected values, still check the SDF and source values.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR is merged and the relevant modification has test coverage; the original author confirmed the alert disappeared after upgrading DART 6.16.6.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does Gazebo Ionic continue to print `Invalid primary/secondary slip compliance (-1)` after upgrade? Should we modify each Fuel model individually?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not use global discarding of Gazebo stderr to mask logs; distinguish between known sentinel regression and actual contact parameter errors.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Confirmed in merged PR: DART 6.16.5's new validation incorrectly treats the negative sentinel as an invalid slip compliance.
translations.details.symptoms.0: About 100 log lines per second of identical warnings; many Fuel models affected; `-v 0` is ineffective.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Maintainer reports Homebrew CI log size increased from <4 MB to over 1.5 GB.
translations.source.locator: Gazebo #3289 author retest 3818259239; merged DART PR #2493
translations.source.title: Gazebo Ionic slip compliance -1 warning storm caused by DART 6.16.5 regression
translations.title: Should we modify each Fuel model individually when Gazebo Ionic 9.5.0 prints many `-1` slip compliance warnings per second?
